summary: The article provides generally accurate information regarding ITR filing for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27) in India, including deadlines, penalties, and verification processes. However, some specific details regarding deadlines for different taxpayer categories and the late filing fee structure could be more precise.

claims.claim: The deadline to file your Income Tax Return (ITR) for the financial year 2025-26 is typically July 31, 2026.
claims.note: For most individual taxpayers not requiring a tax audit, the due date to file the ITR for FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27) is 31st July 2026 for ITR-1 & ITR-2. However, for non-audit ITR-3 & ITR-4 filers, it is August 31, 2026.

claims.claim: After filing, you must verify your ITR within 30 days.
claims.note: The time-limit for e-verification or submission of ITR-V is 30 days from the date of filing the return of income.

claims.claim: Failing to file your ITR by the deadline can result in a late filing fee. This can be up to ₹5,000 if your total income exceeds ₹5 lakh, or ₹1,000 if your income is up to ₹5 lakh, provided you file by December 31st of the assessment year.
claims.note: As per Section 234F, if the return is furnished on or before 31st December of the assessment year, a fee of ₹5,000 is levied. However, if the total income does not exceed ₹5 lakhs, the fee is ₹1,000.

claims.claim: Even if you have no tax liability, filing might still be mandatory if your gross total income (before deductions) is above the basic exemption limit (₹2.5 lakh for those below 60 years under the old tax regime).
claims.note: Under Section 139(1), filing is mandatory for individuals whose total income (before certain deductions) exceeds the basic exemption limit. For individuals below 60 years under the old tax regime, this limit is ₹2.5 lakh.

claims.claim: Also, if you meet certain conditions, such as depositing over ₹1 crore in a current account, spending over ₹2 lakh on foreign travel, or paying electricity bills exceeding ₹1 lakh in a year, filing is compulsory regardless of income.
claims.note: Section 139(1) of the Income Tax Act includes conditions for mandatory filing even if income is below the basic exemption limit, such as depositing ₹1 crore or more in a current account, spending over ₹2 lakh on foreign travel, or electricity bills exceeding ₹1 lakh.

claims.claim: If you miss the deadline, you can still file a "belated return," usually by December 31st of the assessment year.
claims.note: A belated return for AY 2026-27 can be furnished on or before December 31, 2026.

article_title: Your Income Tax Return (ITR) Deadline is Near!
